Synopsis:
Marty Fridson identifies a structural pricing anomaly in investment-grade corporate bonds driven by massive AI-related debt issuance from hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) and Nvidia. Contrary to established credit market norms — where larger, more liquid bonds should trade tighter — recently issued, larger bonds ($3.5–4.0B) from these issuers carry 15–22bps wider spreads than smaller, older comparable bonds. The culprit is market indigestion from an unprecedented supply of mega-sized issues arriving in rapid succession, compounded by institutional diversification constraints and AI investment return uncertainty. With hyperscaler debt supply expected to continue growing, these anomalies risk deepening, potentially impairing the credit market's core function of efficient capital allocation.
